newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FRONTEC '97 earnings to return to black.
newsitem.headline: FRONTEC '97 earnings to return to black.

text.p: Swedish information technology company Frontec expects its earnings to return to the black in fiscal 1997, Carl Gritzmaker, senior vice president, sales & business development said on Tuesday.
When asked if Frontec would return to profitability in fiscal 1997 after expecting to report a loss for fiscal 1996, Gritzmaker said: "Yes."
Frontec officials had previously said the group expected to report a loss for the financial year ended December 1996.
Gritzmaker told Reuters in an interview that 1996's loss would be due to the investments the company made in expanding the business of its AMT or software division globally.
Frontec is expected to report its 1996 results on February 28, officials said.
The company reported a loss of 22 million Swedish crowns for the first half in 1996, with a loss of SKr 0.95 per share.
For the finanical year ended December 1995, Frontec recorded a net attributable profit of SKr 30 million on turnover of about Skr 573 million.
Gritzmaker said the AMT software products division was expected to be profitable in 1997 as well.
The AMT division now had a U.S. headquarters, a regional office in Singapore for the Asia Pacific market and a China representative office.
The AMT division supplies electronic messaging software for industry use, electronic commerce and the Internet.
